paper.title: Adaptive Exploration in Linear Contextual Bandit

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic K-armed contextual linear bandit with M discrete contexts (lower bound)
unmapped: Contexts drawn i.i.d. from an unknown distribution p over [M], each with positive probability; each context m has a known action set A^m of size K
settings.definition_quote: We consider the stochastic $K$-armed contextual linear bandit with a horizon of $n$ rounds and $M$ possible contexts. ... For each context $m \in [M]$ there is a known feature/action set $\cA^m\subset \mathbb R^d$ with $|\cA^m| = K$. ... the environment samples a sequence of independent contexts $(c_t)_{t=1}^n$ from an unknown distribution $p$ over $[M]$ ... $Y_t = \langle X_t,\theta \rangle + \eta_t$, where $(\eta_t)$ is a sequence of independent standard Gaussian random variables ... we assume each $\cA^{m}$ spans $\mathbb R^d$ and $\|x\|_2\leq1$.

source.label: thm:lower_bound
source.quote: Under the same conditions as \cref{lemma:confidence_width}, \liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{R_{\theta}^{\pi}(n)}{\log(n)}\geq \cC(\theta,\cA^1,\ldots, \cA^M), where $\cC$ is defined as the optimal value of the following optimisation problem...

results.notes: Regret defined via <x*_{c_t},theta> minus expected rewards, i.e. pseudo-regret against per-context optimal arm. C equals 0 when optimal arms span R^d (sub-logarithmic regret). Reduces to Lai-Robbins sum 2/Delta for MAB (Example 7).

symbols.C_lin: C(theta, A^1,...,A^M) as defined in Theorem 3

conditions: T_x^m(Delta) uniquely defined and continuous at Delta for all contexts m and actions x

source.label: thm:upper_bound
source.quote: Suppose that $T_x^m(\Delta)$ is uniquely defined and $T_x^m(\cdot)$ is continuous at $\Delta$ for all contexts $m$ and actions $x \in \cA^m$. Then the policy $\pi_{\text{oam}}$ proposed in Algorithm \ref{alg:main} with $\epsilon_t = 1/\log(\log(t))$ satisfies \limsup_{n\to \infty}\frac{R_{\theta}^{\pi_{\text{oam}}}(n)}{\log (n)}\leq \cC(\theta, \cA^1,\ldots, \cA^M).

results.notes: Algorithm uses f_n depending on n, so horizon known. Compute: solves convex optimisation per round (CVXPY), treated as polynomial. Paper notes uniqueness implies continuity (Lemma 27).

conditions: the optimal arms {x_1^*, ..., x_M^*} span R^d
tuning: beta_t = O(d log t) chosen so that P(||theta_hat_t - theta||_{G_t} >= beta_t) <= 1/t^3

source.label: thm:ucb
source.quote: Consider the policy $\pi$ that plays optimistically by $X_t = \argmax_{x \in \cA^{c_t}} \ip{\hat \theta_{t-1}, x} + \|x\|_{G_t^{-1}} \beta_t^{1/2}$. Suppose that $\theta$ is such that $\{x_1^*, \ldots, x_M^*\}$ spans $\mathbb R^d$. Then, for suitable $(\beta_t)_{t=1}^n$ with $\beta_t = O(d \log(t))$, it holds that $\limsup_{n\to\infty} R_\theta^\pi(n) < \infty$.

results.notes: Bounded (finite) asymptotic regret; constant not stated, recorded as O(1). Setting s2 includes T in learner_knows for OAM, but LinUCB does not need T.

cited_results.setting_description: Classical K-armed bandit with unit-variance Gaussian rewards (M=1, standard basis action set), consistent policies
